title: ‘Fellow-servants’ still fits dulia: Scripture’s honorable subjection (Galatians 5) and imperfect ‘service’ by example and intercession
source_text: VI. Quod autem non simus Sanctorum proprie servi, sed conservi, non obstat, ex eorum sensu, quominus Duliae vox apta sit ad significandam observantiam qua Sanctos colimus, quia in Scripturis Dulia non solum accipitur pro servitute mancipiorum, sed etiam pro honoraria subjectione, ut quum dicit Apostolus per charitatem duleuete servite invicem, Galat. 5. Jam vero, quanquam non simus Sanctorum mancipia; quodam tamen imperfecto sensu Sanctorum servi sumus, quatenus illi nos movent & juvant ad bene operandum exemplo suo, & intercessione apud Deum. Ac praeterea quoniam ratione majestatis & gloriae quam possident, nos qui adhuc peregrinamur a Domino multo sumus eis inferiores.
pass_a_gloss: But that we are not properly servants of the Saints, but fellow-servants, does not hinder, on their sense, that the voice Dulia be apt for signifying the observance by which we cultivate the Saints, because in the Scriptures Dulia is taken not only for the servitude of bond-slaves, but also for honorary subjection, as when the Apostle says through charity serve one another, Galatians 5. Now indeed, although we are not the Saints’ bond-slaves; yet in a certain imperfect sense we are servants of the Saints, inasmuch as they move and help us to work well by their example, and by intercession with God. And furthermore because by reason of the majesty and glory which they possess, we who still sojourn from the Lord are much inferior to them.
pass_b_english: Being conservi does not bar dulia: Scripture also uses dulia for honorable subjection—“through love serve one another” (Galatians 5:13).
Imperfectly we are their servants by their example and intercession—and by the majesty and glory that still outrank us pilgrims.

choices.why: Paul’s Galatians wording undergirds honorary dulia.
